card.name: Chozhikali
card.tagline: Central Kerala masked harvest folk play of social satire
card.profile: Chozhikali (also Chozhi Kali / Chozikettu) is a folk dance of central Kerala, mainly the Valluvanad region of Palakkad and Thrissur districts, performed in two forms - Thiruvathirachozhi and Kudachozhi (also called Visharikali) (Wikipedia; Kerala Department of Cultural Affairs). Children dressed as the 'Chozhi' cover their bodies in dried banana and other leaves with masks of areca-palm petiole; the cast includes Yama, Chitragupta and the figure Muthi/Muthiyamma, enacting Yama's attempt to take Muthi to the afterlife (Wikipedia). Songs draw on the Ramayana and Mahabharata, accompanied by chenda and elathalam; Kudachozhi is performed by Pulaya-community families holding a palm-leaf umbrella and a bamboo stick as sword and shield (Wikipedia; Kerala Tourism).
card.insight: Chozhikali is now read as a subaltern art that satirically recreates the world of inequalities experienced during feudal times, with the umbrella and broom serving as symbols of power (Wikipedia).
